title: Direct conversion of human endothelial cells to hepatic progenitor cells
protocol: Plate 1.8 × 10^6 Plat-GP cells on poly-L-lysine-coated 10 cm dishes and culture them in DMEM containing 8% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 2 mM L-glutamine, and penicillin/streptomycin for 3 days.
Dilute PEI (36 µL of 1 mg/mL) with retroviral plasmid DNA (10 µg; FOXA3, HNF1A, and HNF6), and VSV-G expression plasmid pCMV-VSV-G (2 µg) in 1 mL of DMEM.
Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add the above mixture to the plated Plat-GP cells drop-by-drop.
Incubate the plate with the mixture at 37°C, with 5% CO2, for 6 hours.
Replace the medium with fresh medium after incubation.
Collect supernatants from the transfected cells 24 hours after replacing the medium.
Replace the medium with fresh medium and continue culturing.
Again, collect supernatants from the transfected cells 24 hours after replacing the medium.
Filter all the collected supernatants through 0.2 µm cellulose acetate filters.
Concentrate the filtered supernatants by centrifugation (10,000 × g for 16 hours at 4°C).
Resuspend the viral pellets in Hanks’ balanced salt solution (1/140 of initial supernatant volume).
Culture HUVECs in HUVEC medium [1:1 mixture of Medium 200, supplemented with LSGS, and FibroLife S2 Comp kit].
Cryopreserve HUVECs following their expansion in culture.
Thaw cryopreserved HUVECs and seed them at a density of 1.5 × 10^4 cells/well in 12-well gelatin-coated plates.
Culture the seeded HUVECs in HUVEC medium for 6 hours, then replace with fresh medium.
Add concentrated viral supernatants and 5 µg/ml protamine sulfate to the culture after 24 hours (5–10% confluency).
Centrifuge the plates at 800 × g for 10 minutes.
Incubate the plates at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for 6 hours, then replace the medium and continue incubation for 18 hours.
Repeat retrovirus infection three times daily over three days.
Replace the medium with hepato-medium (plus) after the fourth infection.
Replate transduced HUVECs on type I collagen-coated 6-well plates after 48 hours.
Passage the cells every 7 days.
Seed HPBECs at 3 × 10^4 per well of type I collagen-coated 48-well plates.
Culture HPBECs in HPBEC medium until they reach 20–30% confluency.
Perform viral infection with FOXA3, HNF1A, and HNF6, with or without L-MYC.
Perform 7 more retrovirus infections for 7 days.
After the 8th infection, replace the medium with a 1:1 mixture of HPBEC medium and hepato-medium (plus).
Replace the medium with hepato-medium (plus) after 2 days.
Ensure the medium is replaced with fresh medium every week.
Passage cells when compact epithelial cell colonies appear more than 1 month after the final infection.
Seed hiHepPCs at 5 × 10^3 per well of PrimeSurface ultra-low attachment 96-well plates coated with poly 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate.

Culture hiHepPCs in a medium composed of a 1:1 mixture of DMEM and F-12, supplemented with insulin, nicotinamide, L-glutamine, b-mercaptoethanol, rhHGF, Forskolin, A8301, Y-27632, and penicillin/streptomycin.
Mix hiHepPCs (1 × 10^5) with 50 μL of Matrigel and plate them on 24-well plates.
Place the plated Matrigel on a HOT PLATE at 37°C until polymerized.
Add adult human bile duct-derived progenitor cell expansion medium to the polymerized Matrigel after it has set.
Collect cystic epithelial spheroids with medium and Matrigel from each well of 24-well plates.
Transfer collected material to 15 ml tubes.
Break spheroids into small pieces by mechanically pipetting.
Wash broken pieces with medium to remove the Matrigel.
Divide washed pieces in half.
Mix divided pieces with new Matrigel.
Resume culturing the mixed pieces.
